summary: Uses a discovery-led mobilisation year to establish the Digital Student Experience Hub through a focused September 2027 first live release, while building the evidence base for wider institutional integration.
detailSummary:
Student App and Journey Integration owns the Digital Student Experience Hub as the student-facing product and shared application platform. During 2026/27, broad discovery and focused delivery happen together. The year has two linked outcomes: students receive a useful first live Hub release in September 2027, and King’s develops an evidence base for which journeys, integrations and capabilities should deepen next.

King’s Edge is the fixed first substantive native product domain. The current first-release hypothesis is a coherent shared student home with King’s Edge, plus useful light-touch access to timetabling and KEATS and a designed student-facing gateway into the separately delivered enquiry-management capability. Discovery may refine the exact mix and access pattern before scope is locked. The first release does not depend on completion of the wider Student Systems and Data programme, the full CRM transformation or a future ServiceNow direction.

The Hub should be delivered responsive web-first, with native packaging considered later only where device capabilities such as notifications or wayfinding create enough value to justify it. Architecturally, the Hub owns the student-facing experience and journey orchestration. Underlying case management or service workflow may later be provided through ServiceNow or another institutional platform; first-release foundations should therefore avoid unnecessary coupling while not waiting for those decisions.

In parallel, Year One discovery maps the wider student-facing digital estate, priority journeys, information architecture, ownership, authoritative information, source-data and content quality, business-process reliability, service ownership, integration readiness and rationalisation opportunities. A small cohort of paid short student visioning and co-design internships provides sustained student involvement in shaping the Hub vision, experience/design principles and prototypes, while wider student research validates and challenges the cohort’s findings. This discovery work is intentionally broader than the first-release build and creates the evidence-led backlog for Years Two and Three.

The Hub itself is a bespoke student-facing aggregation, journey-orchestration and intelligence layer over authoritative institutional systems. Existing systems remain authoritative where appropriate; the Hub progressively integrates and surfaces the data and functionality students need through coherent journeys rather than wholesale replatforming the source estate.

caseForChange.problem:
Students currently encounter King’s through a fragmented collection of portals, applications, websites and organisational routes. Information and functionality are structured around the systems and teams that provide them rather than around what a student is trying to do. Common needs such as seeing a timetable, entering learning spaces, finding opportunities or asking for support require students to know which destination to use.

The underlying digital estate will remain complex while core systems, data foundations and service platforms evolve. King’s therefore needs a coherent student-facing layer that can create visible value before every underlying dependency is mature.
caseForChange.opportunity:
The Digital Student Experience Hub can provide a bespoke student-facing aggregation, journey-orchestration and intelligence layer across the existing estate. King’s Edge gives the programme a substantive live product domain through which shared foundations can be established and tested. Tightly scoped access to timetabling, KEATS and enquiry management can make the first release useful without creating several parallel integration programmes.

Broad discovery can then identify the priority journeys, information and systems that should deepen next, including whether source data, content ownership, business processes and service operations are sufficiently reliable to support deeper integration. This allows later investment and rationalisation decisions to be made from evidence.
caseForChange.whyNow:
King’s Edge is moving into rapid replatforming and substantial product development, creating a practical opportunity to establish the shared application foundations from which the wider Hub can grow. At the same time, CRM, student systems, data, student-service and potential ServiceNow work are advancing through related institutional programmes. Aligning these now reduces the risk of another generation of disconnected student-facing products.

A focused September 2027 release creates tangible student value and a credible institutional direction while the broader discovery work establishes the roadmap for the remainder of the three-year mobilisation.
caseForChange.intendedChange:
From September 2027, students have one coherent digital place from which to begin their day at King’s. The Digital Student Experience Hub provides a shared home and reusable application layer. King’s Edge is the first substantive native product domain, while timetabling, KEATS and the student-enquiry gateway are represented through the simplest useful and supportable access patterns confirmed through discovery.

By the same point, King’s has mapped the wider student-facing digital estate and priority journeys sufficiently to make evidence-led choices about the next phase. Broader journeys are integrated progressively as student value, service readiness, source-data quality, authoritative ownership, APIs, business-process reliability and CRM capability justify them. Parallel entry points are rationalised where replacement functionality and continuity are proven.

benefits.title: Students have one useful place to start their day
benefits.statement: A coherent digital home gives students clear routes into learning, opportunities, support and essential information without requiring them to understand the institutional systems behind them.
benefits.realisationPeriod: From the September 2027 first release, strengthening as the Hub deepens
benefits.successLooksLike: Students can complete priority navigation and access tasks successfully and report that the Hub is a useful and easy starting point.

benefits.title: Access to provision becomes more equitable
benefits.statement: A consistent digital starting point and clearer discovery routes make services, learning information and opportunities more visible to students who are less able to rely on informal knowledge, confidence or existing networks.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, particularly those currently less well served by fragmented provision
benefits.realisationPeriod: From the first release, increasing as personalisation and integration mature
benefits.successLooksLike: Relevant provision reaches a broader range of students and differences in discovery, navigation or take-up between student groups begin to narrow.

benefits.title: King’s creates a reusable digital student-experience foundation
benefits.statement: A bespoke Hub shell, identity, navigation, journey-orchestration and telemetry layer allows new student-facing journeys to reuse common foundations while authoritative source systems and underlying workflow platforms remain in place where appropriate.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, product teams and King’s
benefits.owner: TBC within SED – enduring Digital Student Experience Hub product owner
benefits.realisationPeriod: From the first live Hub release and as common capabilities are reused
benefits.successLooksLike: New student-facing requirements reuse Hub foundations where appropriate, and deeper integration is added selectively rather than through repeated standalone products.

steps.title: Confirm the first-release hypotheses and access patterns
steps.summary: From September to December 2026, test the current hypothesis for the September 2027 release: King’s Edge as the deep native domain, with timetabling, KEATS and the student-enquiry gateway represented through the simplest safe and useful access patterns. Discovery can refine the precise mix before scope is locked and should identify any future ServiceNow touchpoints without making them prerequisites.

steps.title: Map the wider digital estate and priority student journeys
steps.summary: From November 2026 to June 2027, undertake broad discovery across the student-facing digital estate, priority journeys, information flows, ownership, authoritative information, source-data and content quality, business-process reliability, service ownership, integration readiness and rationalisation opportunities. Include a small paid student visioning and co-design internship cohort to create a student-led vision and design principles, while wider research tests representativeness. Produce the evidence-led wider-Hub backlog without widening the first-release build.

steps.title: Establish the shared app architecture and platform foundations
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish the minimum responsive web-first bespoke Hub architecture, hosting, identity, navigation, student-facing journey orchestration, telemetry and service foundations needed for the King’s Edge replatform and focused first release. Keep the boundary with future ServiceNow or other underlying workflow capability explicit so the Hub can evolve without significant rework.

steps.title: Prototype the common student home
steps.summary: From November 2026 to April 2027, test increasingly realistic versions of the responsive shared home with students, using the paid co-design internship cohort for sustained visioning and design work and wider student research for validation. Focus on information hierarchy, navigation, the relationship between King’s Edge and the lighter-touch institutional journeys, and whether the Hub is genuinely useful as a starting point.

steps.title: Build the shared Hub shell alongside King’s Edge
steps.summary: From January to June 2027, build the responsive common home, identity, navigation, profile, student-facing journey orchestration and telemetry while the deeper King’s Edge product develops under 4.1.4. Implement only the timetable, KEATS and student-enquiry gateway access justified for the focused first release.

steps.title: Test the working Hub with students and service owners
steps.summary: From March to June 2027, test the working common home with a bounded but varied student cohort and relevant service owners, focusing on usefulness, task success, clarity, accessibility and hand-offs.

steps.title: Lock the September first-release scope and Year Two priorities
steps.summary: By the end of June 2027, use product testing and the broader discovery evidence to confirm the minimum September release and an evidence-led priority backlog for the next phase.

steps.title: Complete proportionate launch readiness
steps.summary: During July and August 2027, complete security, privacy, accessibility, performance, monitoring, support and release-readiness work appropriate to the confirmed first-release scope while protecting King’s Edge service continuity.

steps.title: Launch the first Digital Student Experience Hub release
steps.summary: Launch in September 2027 with a coherent shared student home, King’s Edge as the substantive native product domain, and the agreed useful access to the other first-release journeys confirmed through discovery.

steps.title: Operate, learn and decide where deeper integration is worth it
steps.summary: From September 2027 to February 2028, use live evidence alongside Year One discovery to improve the Hub, establish baseline measures and identify where deeper integration would create enough student value to justify additional product, service and technical effort.

steps.title: Approve the deeper roadmap and first end-to-end non-Edge journeys
steps.summary: From March to April 2028, combine live Hub evidence, the wider digital-estate and journey discovery, and learning from King’s Edge to select the first non-Edge areas that should move beyond access and hand-off into deeper integrated journeys.

steps.title: Deepen the Hub with the first end-to-end non-Edge journeys
steps.summary: Build the first selected deeper journeys into the existing Hub, connecting authoritative data and CRM- or ServiceNow-enabled interactions where ready while retaining specialist source systems where they continue to add value.

steps.title: Expand integrated journeys and common Hub capabilities
steps.summary: Add further priority journeys and mature common search, actions, communications, notifications, personalisation, self-service and system integration, progressively replacing shallow hand-offs where deeper integration adds clear value.

steps.title: Make wider student journeys the primary product roadmap
steps.summary: By the end of the three-year mobilisation, establish the Hub as a broad institutional product with a substantial range of integrated journeys, mature governance and an evidence-led ongoing roadmap.

steps.title: Continue product development and rationalise proven redundant entry points
steps.summary: After mobilisation, continue to deepen the Hub and progressively retire or consolidate redundant student-facing entry points where replacement functionality, service continuity and enduring ownership are proven.
